question: Which small JVM programs give the most syscall + JIT coverage per wall-second under `hermit run --strict --verify`, so we can keep meaningful JVM validation on every commit without javac's cost?
host_load_caveat: The host ran many concurrent Hermit workloads from other agents during the hermit pass; absolute wall times are inflated upper bounds. Relative ranking is the reliable signal.
jdk: OpenJDK 1.8.0_492 (Temurin), 64-Bit Server VM, tiered compilation ON

native_pass.syscalls: strace -f -c java <args>  (unique = distinct syscall rows, total = sum of calls column, threads followed)
native_pass.wall: min of 3 native runs, JIT ON

hermit_pass.preemption: RCB preemption DEFAULT ON (NO --max-timeslice=disabled) — required so JIT-on compute threads are preempted; --max-timeslice=disabled livelocks compute-bound JVMs
hermit_pass.jit: ON (no -Xint) for realistic runtime + JIT surface
